title: How the day closed
text: It was a rough day. All 17 names on our list closed lower. The S&P 500 fund (SPY) fell 2.0% and the Nasdaq 100 fund (QQQ) fell 2.2%. Anthropic had a strong first day on the stock market, but that was not enough to lift everything else. AI chip stocks were hit hardest: our 'AI supplies' group fell about 4.2% on average, while the 'AI giants' group fell about 3.1%.

title: AMD had the biggest drop
text: AMD fell 7.7% today, the largest drop on our list. Vertiv, which makes power and cooling gear for data centers, fell 4.8%. Both had risen a lot earlier this month, so they can also fall fast when investors get nervous. AMD's risk score is 7.6 out of 10 (High).

title: NVIDIA and Alphabet sit at their 52 week lows
text: NVIDIA closed at $145.98, almost exactly its lowest price of the past year ($145.71). Alphabet closed at $272.66, right next to its low of $272.11. Both are about 33% to 40% below their highs. Being near a low does not mean a stock must bounce. It only tells us where the price sits compared with the past year.

title: Calm stocks fell less
text: Lockheed Martin fell only 1.1% and the dividend fund SCHD fell 1.5%. These companies tend to move less than the market (Lockheed's beta is close to zero). On days like today, that is the point of owning some steadier names next to the exciting ones.

title: Long term interest rates stay high
text: The 10 year Treasury yield averaged 5.13% in October, up from 4.09% a year earlier. Higher rates make borrowing more expensive and make safe bonds more attractive compared with stocks. That pressure is part of the backdrop for this month's slide in fast growing tech stocks.

title: Lesson 59: What is market breadth?
text: Market breadth tells us how many stocks are joining a move, not just how far an index moved. If the index falls but only a few big stocks are dropping, breadth is narrow. If almost everything falls, breadth is broad. Today was broad: AP reported that more than 90% of the stocks in the S&P 500 were down late in the day, and every name on our list fell. Broad selloffs usually come from big worries that touch the whole market, like interest rates or fear about AI spending, rather than news about one company.

title: What this covers
text: Prices, daily changes, beta and 52 week ranges for all 17 names come from the close on November 19, 2026. Analyst price targets and company ratios were updated today for NVIDIA, TSMC, AMD, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, GE Aerospace and Lockheed Martin. The other names have no targets on our free data plan. Treasury data runs through October 2026. This is information for learning, not advice to buy or sell.
